statement: For the linear function $f$, $f(4) = 3f(1)$ and $f(6) = 26$. What is the value of $f(0)$?

choices.misconception: I found $f(x) = 4x + 2$ correctly but gave the slope, 4, instead of $f(0)$.
I got the relationship backwards and wrote $b = 2m$ instead of $m = 2b$, so $6m + b = 26$ became $4b = 26$ and $b = 6.5$.
I wrote $3f(1)$ as $3m + b$ instead of $3(m + b)$, which made the slope 0, so $f$ was the constant 26.

hints: Write $f(x) = mx + b$ and turn each fact into an equation.
$f(4) = 3f(1)$ becomes $4m + b = 3(m + b)$. Simplify it to relate $m$ and $b$, then use $f(6) = 26$.
$4m + b = 3m + 3b$ gives $m = 2b$. Then $6m + b = 26$ becomes $12b + b = 26$.

solutions.reliable: Let $f(x) = mx + b$. Then $f(4) = 4m + b$ and $3f(1) = 3m + 3b$. Setting them equal gives $m = 2b$. From $f(6) = 26$: $6m + b = 26$, so $12b + b = 13b = 26$ and $b = 2$, $m = 4$. So $f(x) = 4x + 2$ and $f(0) = 2$. Check: $f(4) = 18 = 3 \cdot 6 = 3f(1)$ and $f(6) = 26$.
